72 hours. That is all it took.

Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5 — its most powerful model — on June 9. By June 12, a US export-control directive forced the company to shut it down for every single customer. Not a bug. Not downtime. A government order.

The jailbreak that triggered the shutdown has been fully documented. The 120,000-character system prompt is now public on GitHub. And the enterprise world is rethinking everything about cloud-dependent AI infrastructure.

At the same time, Anthropic filed a confidential S-1 with the SEC. President Daniela Amodei said openly that compute costs are pushing the company toward an IPO. Public markets will add new pressures to how Anthropic releases models, sets prices, and invests in safety.

For executives who built critical workflows on frontier AI models, this is the wake-up call. The risk is no longer just technical. It is regulatory, geopolitical, and financial — all at once.

The organizations that build resilience into their AI architecture now will absorb these disruptions. The ones that do not will scramble.
